title: Sovereign tenant policy enforcer + KMS affinity gate
author: Anika Patel
description:
Problem/context: customers running in highly regulated regions asked for a single enforcement point that guarantees tenant-level data residency and cryptographic key affinity at admission time. Existing RBAC v2 checks and KMS scoping lived in separate layers which led to occasional races where a request could be evaluated by RBAC before KMS-affinity policy was applied (see incident SUP-7780). This PR introduces a policy enforcer that runs as a deterministic admission filter in the fronting API router and a KMS affinity gating module that enforces key-location pinning and rejects requests that would violate tenant_region or sovereign_profile constraints.

Solution summary: add a new policy-enforcer component (pkg/policy/enforcer) that materializes tenant sovereignty rules, validates request attributes (tenant_id, region_hint, kms_cmk_hint, service_role), and emits a signed admission token for downstream services. Integrate a KMS affinity gate (pkg/kms/affinity_gate) that consumes the admission token and performs a deterministic check against the tenant's registered CMK location and the configured residency policy. The gate supports soft-fallback (log+warn) when in permissive mode, and hard-enforce reject for enforced tenants.

What this PR does (implementation highlights):
- Introduces API contract: api/v1/tenant_policy.proto defines TenantPolicy, AffinityMode, and SignedAdmissionEnvelope. The envelope includes a short-lived signature to attest that the enforcer validated residency parameters.
- New runtime component: pkg/policy/enforcer implements policy matching, prefix-allowlists, and enrichment with audit tags (sovereign_tenant, region_pin, policy_version).
- KMS affinity gating: pkg/kms/affinity_gate checks incoming requests' admission envelopes and verifies CMK location via KMS metadata cache. If mismatch and affinity=ENFORCE -> request rejected with 403 and audit reason. If affinity=PERMISSIVE -> request allowed but emits audit with severity=warning.
- Migration path: feature flags and tenant opt-in. Default behavior for existing tenants is permissive to avoid regressions.
- Observability: adds metrics (policy_enforcer.evaluations_total, affinity_gate.rejections_total), a tracing span with tenant and region tags, and enriched audit log entries for downstream retention.
- Tests: unit tests for policy matching, integration tests that exercise signed admission envelopes and simulated KMS metadata responses, and a small e2e scenario under perf-canary to validate latency impact (aim: <1ms p50 extra on admission path).

- [x] Audit entries added with immutable tags
- [x] CI unit and integration tests passing
- [x] Docs/console migration guide added (docs/sovereign-policy.md)

Notes on forward compatibility and safety: SignedAdmissionEnvelope is additive and optional; services that do not validate it will continue to function. The policy enforcer runs as a pre-routing filter in the API router so it can short-circuit early and emit audit logs before downstream processing (reduces blast radius). The KMS affinity gate consults a cached CMK location and falls back to an authoritative KMS metadata endpoint with exponential backoff.

Migration plan for customers: default permissive for all existing tenants; productctl/console will have a toggle per-tenant to switch to ENFORCE mode. We included a dry-run mode (report-only) to help customers identify mismatches before flipping enforcement.

review_comments: Ethan Morris: Overall approach looks good. Two asks: 1) add a short TTL to SignedAdmissionEnvelope (recommend 30s) to limit replay, 2) include a stable policy_version string so downstream can detect policy drift. Please address.
Anika Patel: Added envelope ttl=30s and policy_version header in latest commit (b2e7a4c). Also documented rotation considerations in docs/sovereign-policy.md.
Sofia Rivera: We need a clear operator fallback if KMS metadata endpoint is unreachable (eg degrade to permissive or fail closed). Can we make that configurable per deployment?

Anika Patel: Added server-side config 'kms_affinity_failure_mode' (per-deployment) with options [permissive, enforce, fail_open]. Default in staging set to permissive. See charts and terraform changes.
Lina Becker: Please add an audit log schema sample in the docs and ensure PII is never included in the signed envelope payload. Also request unit test covering rejection path for ENFORCE mode.
Anika Patel: Added docs sample and added test 'TestAffinityGateRejectsMismatchedCMK' in tests/integration.
merge: merged by Sofia Rivera via squash-merge
release_notes: Add sovereign tenant policy enforcer and KMS affinity gate. Default permissive mode for existing tenants. New audit fields and metrics. See docs/sovereign-policy.md for migration steps.
notes_for_ops: When enabling ENFORCE for a tenant, run the dry-run report first and validate there are zero mismatches. If KMS metadata service is degraded, operator can set kms_affinity_failure_mode=permissive to avoid customer impact. Rolling restart of api-router required to flip feature flag cluster-wide.
security_considerations: SignedAdmissionEnvelope uses current signing key rotation and is short-lived to mitigate replay. Enforcer filters at admission time and adds immutable audit tags. Do not include tenant PII in envelope payload. All KMS metadata queries are performed with service-level credentials and logged at info level only; sensitive fields are redacted.
testing_instructions: 1) enable feature flag in staging as permissive. 2) opt-in tenant via console toggle. 3) run tests/integration/sovereign_policy_test.go. 4) flip tenant to ENFORCE and verify request with mismatched CMK returns 403 and emits audit entry with reason 'KMS_AFFINITY_MISMATCH'.
